newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian City Hotels focuses on rundown U.S. hotels.
newsitem.headline: Belgian City Hotels focuses on rundown U.S. hotels.

text.p: Victor Hasson, chairman of Belgian hotels and airline group City Hotels, said on Thursday that his company wanted to expand its hotel business in the United States -- partly by buying ones that are run down.

"Our strategy is not the same as five years ago. Now all (U.S.) hotels do better and they have become too expensive. We've never bought during a boom," Hasson told a news conference to present a one billion Belgian franc convertible bond issue.
He said that City Hotels instead decided to buy "derelict hotels, I mean hotels that need serious renovating".

"We can buy them now because they belong to owners in distress, who can get a reasonable price...the idea is that we buy an old hotel, put in nearly just as much to renovate it...and in the longer run we hope to obtain a capital gain of between 50 and 100 percent," he said.
The only condition was that the hotels had to be located in areas with strong growth potential, he said.

City Hotels, which also owns the fledgling long-haul airline City Bird, launched its five-year bond issue to raise funds to develop its U.S. hotel business, which has been its main growth area for hotel activities since 1993.

The company already booked considerable capital gains on the sale of three hotels that it acquired in 1993 and 1995. But the sale also cut its hotel capacity in the United States to 1,545 rooms from 2,196.

Hasson said that City Hotels, which also operates hotels in Belgium and the Netherlands, plans to invest about $100 million in the U.S. in the next two years by buying existing hotels and building some new ones.
"It's much easier to operate hotels in the U.S. than in Europe," he said.

Factors which made the U.S. market more attractive include its higher liquidity, lower fixed operating costs and lower fiscal pressure. In addition prices were more calculated in terms of potential profit, he added.
He said the change in strategy for the U.S. had been prompted by a recovery in the U.S. hotel sector.
Hasson said he was close to deciding to buy the Royce hotel in Detroit and had bid $7.25 million.
He also offered $4.6 million to take over the Radisson hotel in Dayton. City Hotels is also eyeing a 202-room beachside hotel in Florida and bidding $13 million for it, he said.
The group also set up a joint venture with a U.S. promoter to build two profitable low-cost Homewood Suites.
City Hotels will invest $10 million in each of the two constructions, which will become operational early 1998. Both are located near airports -- one near Dulles.
Hasson added he was not excluding acquisitions of hotels in Europe.
